part: Upright bare J5 4P relay-ribbon clip coupon on a 3 mm host wall
status: Print deformation reported; cancelled before completion
authority: Derek, direct physical report and two photographs in chat
print_pose_at_preparation: Entry-up STL, with no rotation. The 24 by 3 mm wall edge starts on the bed; the 45 degree hook corbel starts 6 mm above it.
observation: So that last one came out pretty melty there. I stopped it partway, as you'll see. So we definitely can't do anything quite like that again without some major part fan cooling and time between layers. So I think I'd like to see that with a 9 millimeter thick wall, and I'd also like to see the hook cavity be a bit longer as far as a longer length of cable within the cavity. And I don't know, maybe you can set it up with a couple variations. I'm going to be going into bed soon, and so I've got the plate cleared for you now, and I'd like to get a test print here that has both what I asked for with the tube snaps and whatever we want to do next here for the cable clips. So prepare a larger test plate of both things, taking into consideration that we're going to be doing this on 9 millimeter thick walls and might need a bit longer cavity.
stop_basis: Direct report that he stopped the print partway; no completion telemetry is inferred from the launch receipt.
visible_photo_observations: Uneven and wavy layer bands on the incomplete coupon.
Localized glossy material buildup and distortion around portions of the partially formed hook.
reported_heat_or_layer_time_interpretati: Derek describes the print as melty and calls for substantially more part-fan cooling and more time between layers.
cause_scope: The photographs and report establish the deformed partial result, not its measured temperature or a uniquely established thermal, cooling or layer-time cause.

requested_next_trial.cable_cavity_length: Longer cable contact span than this coupon
requested_next_trial.cooling_and_layer_time: More part-fan cooling and more time between layers requested
